summary: Enforce explicit PostgreSQL tenant and narrowly scoped platform execution contexts, preserve identity and administrator workflows, and deliver optional hash-bound configuration exclusively to the API.
userImpact: Operators can configure platform identity bootstrap without sharing its credential with workers or database jobs.
Pooled PostgreSQL workloads now fail closed when tenant or verified platform context is absent; deployment requires a coordinated security upgrade.

instructions: Before migration 1700000000131, upgrade or drain every API, worker and retained-release consumer of the shared PostgreSQL schema. Older consumers cannot remain active against the new policies.
Use the dedicated schema-owner migration transport and a restricted nonowning runtime role without role memberships; runtime startup rejects privileged application credentials.

The apiConfigBundle chart delivery remains disabled by default and is separate from mandatory PostgreSQL policy enforcement. Qualify validate mode and restricted-role bootstrap before explicitly enabling apply mode.
Preserve tenant and business identifiers. Do not compensate for an incomplete coordinated upgrade by disabling RLS, granting owner credentials or adding permissive policies.

configuration: Host chart 0.1.20 to 0.1.21 adds optional apiConfigBundle with an existing ConfigMap key, exact SHA-256, validate/apply mode and one existing Secret key. The credential is exposed only as EG_CONFIG_BUNDLE_SECRET in the API container.
The frontend-host patch is dependency-only because its packed workspace dependency resolves the new shared package; no frontend UI source change is included.

changes: No REST endpoint or wire schema is changed. Existing verified identity, session, manual administrator and deactivation commands retain their authorization boundaries.
The breaking impact is operational PostgreSQL enforcement, independently of the additive optional chart configuration.

notes: PostgreSQL FORCE-RLS requires four canonical command policies per managed table. Owner-written catalog attestations bind source and parsed predicates, detecting same-name USING/WITH CHECK broadening, missing/stale attestations, and extra permissive policies; this is drift detection, not a signature against a schema owner.
The TypeORM boundary serializes runner context, clears it on success and failure, and rejects unsafe reuse or privileged runtime identities.
Runtime configuration reconciliation persists terminal task CAS and its receipt in one short transaction; external reconciliation remains outside the database transaction.
Other database engines do not execute this PostgreSQL policy migration; PostgreSQL verification alone is not cross-database compatibility acceptance.

security: The bundle is read-only, hash-verified and fail-closed with required secret preflight. No additional environment or volume is inherited by frontend, workers, migration, preflight or Plugin Manager.
Platform operations use finite revocable capabilities after protocol or service authorization; global rows have no blanket null-tenant exception.
Manual administrator grant/revoke cannot modify source-managed assignments. Password-verified recovery claims bind the complete existing membership snapshot and allow only an unchanged row.
Baseline revocation requires the canonical inactive user locked in the deactivation transaction, including SCIM lifecycle paths.
knownLimitations: Kubernetes resource existence, secret availability and external provider registration require deployment acceptance; chart rendering and local signed-protocol fixtures are not a live consent journey.
Pooled streaming and global identity/runtime queue continuations remain unsupported. Existing global task rows are not claimed as processed.
Tenant queue cursors provide fairness only during a worker process lifetime; restart resets the cursor and this is not durable or cross-replica scheduling.

Shared-engine readiness is a successful reconciliation snapshot. Later tenant lifecycle changes do not automatically invalidate that cached snapshot; request-time tenant authorization remains independent.
rollback: There is no in-place PostgreSQL down migration restoring permissive policies. Rollback requires the qualified pre-upgrade backup and compatible runtime; restoring that backup loses subsequent writes.
Disabling optional chart delivery removes the API mount and secret environment but does not undo persisted provider configuration or mandatory policy enforcement.
validation: Focused API-only chart rendering and negative schema/isolation checks cover credential noninheritance.

Restricted PostgreSQL 16 integration exercises real signed OIDC verification, callback/session persistence, provider bootstrap receipt replay, administrator mutations and denials, recovery password verification, transactional rollback, and baseline deactivation/reactivation.
Focused tenant queue, SCIM ordering, bootstrap and administrator regressions run locally; complete the relevant protected and historical database qualification at the release milestone.
